key_insight: Superfluid helium-4 still exhibits a logarithmic law of the wall, but with a distinctly nonclassical, reduced Kármán constant that stays nearly temperature-invariant, implying strong coupling between the normal and superfluid components.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical near-wall flow law for He II, helping improve the design and operation of cryogenic cooling and transport systems.
method: Molecular tagging velocimetry to visualize near-wall velocity in mechanically driven He II pipe flow
Independent wall-shear-stress estimation from pressure-drop measurements
Comparison of wall profiles across temperatures and Reynolds numbers up to 1.26×10^6
evidence_signal: The abstract reports robust logarithmic velocity profiles in the normal-fluid component across the tested range, with a Kármán constant less than half the classical value and nearly unchanged with temperature.
watch_item: The observed wall law is specific to the measured pipe-flow regime and temperature range, so broader applicability to other geometries or flow states should be validated before use in design.
paper_title: A nonclassical law of the wall in superfluid helium-4
